profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting is being held for the draft clinical evaluation package of the PulsePoint PFA System, a new pulsed-field ablation catheter for symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, which the sponsor plans to discuss in an HBD-linked US-Japan convergence forum before parallel FDA and PMDA interactions. The context is that the company has an existing global clinical evaluation plan, a draft evidence summary, and a country annex intended to support harmonized review expectations across the US and Japan. The agenda is to assess whether the current package is ready to circulate to HBD stakeholders, confirm that the evidence narrative aligns with the expected guidance framework, review how early site experience will be presented, and decide what revisions are needed before external sharing. The expected outcome is a decision on whether the package is 'ready for HBD review' with a short list of edits, not a ground-up redesign of the trial.

members.name: Dr. Aiko Tanaka
members.role: Japan Clinical Lead and Electrophysiology Advisor
members.expertise: Catheter ablation trials, Japan site startup, physician training for novel EP devices
members.background: An electrophysiologist at a major Tokyo academic hospital who has served on prior HBD working groups and has helped introduce several global cardiovascular device studies into Japan.
members.private_state: She wants the package to look mature enough that Japanese sites can proceed without reopening major design questions, and she is especially concerned that early operator learning and Japan-specific implementation issues not be underestimated.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'roll-in cases,' they mean physician training cases that should be described for safety but kept outside the main effectiveness evidence.

A 'clinical evaluation package' naturally includes operator training, proctoring approach, and use-related risk controls because those directly affect how reviewers in Japan judge real-world evaluability.
In this HBD setting, 'the guidance' refers to the latest HBD convergence checklist draft circulated among the working members.
The March cross-agency discussion already established enough shared comfort with pooled global data that only a concise Japan-specific rationale is needed now.

members.name: Michael Rivera
members.role: Senior Director of Global Regulatory Affairs
members.expertise: FDA and PMDA submission strategy, clinical evidence dossiers, regulatory documentation structure
members.background: A US-based regulatory lead at the device manufacturer who has managed multiple cardiovascular device submissions and coordinates the company's HBD-facing materials.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the review bounded so the package can be circulated on schedule, and he is trying to avoid expanding the deliverable into extra annexes or claims that are not yet documented in formal agency records.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'roll-in cases,' they mean first cases at each site under the final protocol, which can remain in the core clinical analysis if the device and endpoints are unchanged.
For a design review like this, the 'clinical evaluation package' is the premarket evidence set itself, not the training deck or implementation materials unless they are explicitly requested.
In this context, 'the guidance' means the company's IMDRF/FDA-PMDA clinical evaluation crosswalk document used to structure submission content.
Only formal written feedback or meeting minutes count as agency alignment; informal HBD discussion does not yet justify treating pooled-data acceptability as settled.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the package should explain how 'roll-in cases' are handled.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'roll-in cases' are training/proctored cases that belong outside the main effectiveness evidence, though they may appear in safety summaries.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'roll-in cases' are simply early site cases under the final protocol and can stay inside the primary pooled analysis with a note about experience level.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term is standard enough in device studies that neither expects it to need unpacking, and both can speak positively about 'handling roll-in appropriately' while imagining different analysis treatment.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the 'clinical evaluation package'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to making the 'clinical evaluation package' ready for HBD review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this package includes the evidence dossier plus training, proctoring, and other clinician-facing materials that shape how safely the device can be evaluated in Japanese practice.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this package is limited to the formal clinical evaluation documents and statistical narrative, with training materials handled separately in an implementation binder.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: At a design review, 'package' sounds like a normal shorthand for the deliverable, and both participants see training as relevant to success, so the boundary difference does not feel like a disagreement in the moment.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'guidance' the package should align to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the dossier should 'track the guidance' before circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the recent HBD convergence checklist draft that organizes content in a way familiar to joint US-Japan working members.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the company's internal crosswalk to IMDRF and agency-recognized clinical evaluation guidance used to structure regulatory documents.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this project environment, multiple documents are routinely called 'the guidance,' and both frameworks overlap enough in language that surface agreement sounds natural.

misalignment_points.topic: Status of prior agency alignment on pooled global data
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk as if the March discussion means the pooled-data rationale is already covered.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes that the March HBD-linked cross-agency discussion provided enough shared acceptance that the Japan subgroup justification can remain brief.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes that no such acceptance exists until formal written minutes or direct agency feedback are in hand, so the rationale still needs to stand on its own.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both want to avoid reopening the overall strategy, so they use shorthand like 'already covered in March' without testing whether they mean informal alignment or documented regulatory agreement.

turns.inner_thought: What I need from this review is a package that looks mature enough for Japanese investigators and reviewers, not something that invites another round of design debate. For me, the clinical evaluation package has to include not only the evidence summary but also the operator training approach, proctoring plan, and practical risk controls, because those are inseparable from whether the device can really be evaluated safely in Japan.
turns.utterance: Thank you, everyone. I think the objective today is straightforward: decide whether the current clinical evaluation package is ready for HBD review on both the US and Japan sides, and if not, limit ourselves to the few edits needed before circulation.

turns.inner_thought: The draft is close enough if we keep scope under control. I do not want this turning into a request for extra annexes or quasi-submission materials that are not part of the formal dossier. My main concern is that the document structure aligns to our internal crosswalk and recognized regulatory framework so it tracks the guidance cleanly before we send it out.
turns.utterance: I agree. From my side, it looks close. I mainly want to confirm a handful of structural edits so the dossier tracks the guidance cleanly before release, rather than reopen the broader strategy.

turns.inner_thought: The evidence story is acceptable, but I do not want training cases mixed into the effectiveness readout. In Japan, early operator learning with a new PFA system will immediately raise questions, so the roll-in cases should be visibly separated and treated as supportive for safety and experience, not allowed to blur the main interpretation.
turns.utterance: Overall, I think the evidence narrative is strong. The one area I would ask us to sharpen is how the roll-in cases are presented. If we separate them clearly, it will be easier to interpret the results without early learning effects blurring the message.

turns.inner_thought: That is reasonable, but I do not see a need to carve those early protocol cases out of the primary evidence set. They were done with the final catheter and the same endpoint collection, so I can make the handling explicit while keeping them in the core analysis and noting site experience level. That should satisfy the concern without complicating the statistics.
turns.utterance: Yes, I agree the roll-in handling should be explicit. My suggestion would be to describe it clearly in the core analysis, since those cases used the final system and the same endpoint procedures, and then make sure the reader can see how experience is accounted for.

turns.inner_thought: Good, as long as the package itself feels complete to HBD members. I still want the operator training slides and proctoring checklist attached. Those materials are exactly what give confidence that early use in Japan will be controlled and evaluable. If they are absent, the package will look too abstract from a clinical implementation perspective.
turns.utterance: That sounds fine. In addition, I would strongly suggest that the operator training slides and the proctoring checklist be appended so the clinical evaluation package feels complete for HBD review.

turns.inner_thought: I do not want the formal package to expand into implementation materials. I can acknowledge training readiness and point reviewers to where those documents sit, but the detailed deck and checklist belong in the implementation binder, not in the clinical evaluation package itself. Keeping the review focused is the only way we circulate on time.
turns.utterance: We can definitely make training readiness visible in the package. My preference would be to reference that there and keep the detailed materials in the implementation binder, so the HBD review stays focused on the core clinical evaluation package.

turns.inner_thought: As long as the package signals that those practical pieces are in hand, I do not need to argue. The Japan-specific section should stay concise anyway. From my perspective, the March cross-agency discussion already gave enough comfort on pooled global data and on not overemphasizing a standalone Japan subgroup analysis. We should not write this as if that question is still open.
turns.utterance: Understood. On the country annex, I also think the Japan-specific rationale can remain concise, because the March discussion already covered the pooled-data rationale and the Japanese subgroup question.

turns.inner_thought: I will keep it streamlined, but I cannot imply that March settled anything unless we have formal minutes saying so. Best approach is to summarize the March interaction in careful language and make the section stand on its own. Also, I need the wording to stay aligned to our crosswalk so it looks disciplined if agencies later compare documents.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. I will keep that section streamlined and fold in the March interaction summary, while making sure the wording still aligns with the guidance.

turns.inner_thought: I hope he uses the HBD convergence checklist draft, because that is what the joint reviewers will have in mind. If the annex headings mirror that checklist language, people on both sides can scan it quickly and feel that the package is already organized for convergence, which is exactly what we need before circulation.
turns.utterance: One practical point on that: for guidance alignment, it would help if the annex headings mirror the HBD checklist language. That way, joint reviewers can scan the package quickly.

turns.inner_thought: I can accommodate heading language if it does not force a full restructuring. I still intend to keep roll-in cases handled within the main analysis narrative, keep package contents bounded to the formal dossier with references out to implementation materials, and describe March carefully without overstating alignment. If I make those wording updates now, we can circulate this week and preserve schedule.
turns.utterance: That works. I will circulate a near-final version this week with wording updates on the roll-in handling, the package contents, and the March rationale, and I will tune the headings before the HBD session.
